description: Every Tauri command the Rust bridge (ui/src-tauri/src/commands/) exposes to the TS connector (ui/src/connector/tauri/tauri-connector.ts). Threading classes: 'sync' (safe to run on the invoking thread — engine any-thread or pure bridge logic), 'spawn-join' (engine call is synchronous-on-caller-thread; the command spawns a dedicated thread and joins/awaits), 'async-job' (spawns a long-running thread; completion arrives via events + state queries). Events are listed separately.

commands.name: scan_start
commands.notes: Spawns the run thread; events on scan-progress:<scanId>; pathScope is view-scoping (G-11) validated here (scan-scope-invalid). Pre-scan repair arms the CONSENT callback (bridge::consent, G-1 (a)): the engine calls it ONCE on the run thread when a repairable plan exists, the bridge emits consent-request:<scanId> + blocks the run thread on the registered gate (no user-facing timeout — plan §4.5), and consent_respond answers. The run tail frees the consent pipe, force-denies any surviving gate, and persists the undo log after an approved repair (cr_ui_scan_repair_save_undo). Virtual quick-targets (vol-recycle-bin / vol-desktop) resolve to the system volume + implicit pathScope

commands.name: scan_cancel
commands.notes: run() latches CR_UI_ERR_CANCELLED -> status 'cancelled' with browsable tree. Force-denies the scan's pending consent gates FIRST: a pending consent blocks the run thread inside the engine callback, and the engine observes the cancel token only after the callback returns (plan §4.5 deadlock rule)

commands.name: scan_state
commands.returns: ScanState (type-maps §3) + pendingConsent (the consent-request payload | null — G-1 (a) re-hydration)
commands.notes: pendingConsent re-hydrates the prompt: the event fired before the page subscribed, or the user navigated away and back. Null when nothing pends (answered, denied, cancelled)

commands.name: scan_close
serves: internal (bridge lifecycle; invoked on window close / session adoption)
commands.notes: Present in the manifest because it is a registered command; the TS connector calls it when leaving a scan surface

commands.name: results_query
commands.notes: ONE bridge-side filter path serves BOTH live scans and loaded sessions: the engine's cr_ui_query_run cannot express the contract's 'existing' atom (no deleted_never knob exists in cr_ui_query), so the bridge filters its own metadata cache for both — identical semantics mid-scan and post-scan; G-7 records the future engine-side query migration

commands.name: preview_open
commands.notes: connector decides kind from engine metadata (ADR-008); bounded payload assembly; the preview handle is transient (opened + closed inside the command — no paging surface exists in the contract, so preview_read/preview_close are internal helpers, not commands)

commands.name: preview_thumbnail
commands.notes: image-kind only; non-image -> null (G-4); oversized images -> null (OQ-3 resolved: full-read bound, no decode fabrication)

commands.name: session_save
commands.notes: path null -> ProgramData auto-name; save progress on save-progress:<scanId>; save-scoped cancel token

commands.name: sessions_list
commands.notes: OQ-4 resolved: stat-first listing; label/target counts filled lazily via one load+close pass per file on first list (cached in the bridge; cache invalidated by directory mtime)

commands.name: recovery_start
commands.notes: enqueue phase = 'validating'; process thread spawned; events on recovery-progress:<jobId>

commands.name: system_driver_status
commands.returns: DriverStatus (type-maps §10; SCM probe + \\.\RDA open + IOCTL GET_VERSION)

commands.name: system_app_info
commands.returns: AppInfo (connectorMode removed; engineVersion null per G-6; abiVersion in detail)

commands.name: system_pick_directory
commands.notes: tauri-plugin-dialog; volume hint root; excludeDeviceId honored

commands.name: system_open_path
commands.notes: tauri-plugin-opener reveal; replaces the staged reveal_in_explorer command and un-wires the mock's openPathMock refusal

commands.name: consent_respond
commands.notes: The consent answer for the pre-scan repair prompt (G-1 (a), plan §4.5). requestId is the ECHO token from the consent-request payload — bridge-minted, never a guessable authority. Unknown / already-resolved / cancelled ids throw the typed consent-not-found. Registry-only (the gate's condvar notifies the blocked engine run thread); no engine call, hence sync. The engine executes the transactional repair on a true return, surfaces the outcome via CR_EVT_REPAIR + stats, and the run tail persists the undo log (rrecov fix --undo-apply <file>)

commands.name: repair_dry_run
commands.notes: G-1 disabled surface: no engine ABI export exists; truthful message + INTEGRATION-GAPS.md pointer

commands.name: repair_apply
commands.notes: G-1: the REAL repair path is pre-scan repair inside scan_start (consent-gated); the standalone workbench button is truthfully disabled

commands.name: repair_undo
commands.notes: G-1 disabled surface; CLI-only today (rrecov fix --undo-apply)

events.name: consent-request:<scanId>
events.source: cr_ui_repair_consent_fn (bridge::consent — the sink emits from the run thread; the gate is registered before emitting and the registry lock released before blocking, plan §4.5)

removed.name: preview_read
removed.why: Internal helper (the bridge's hex assembly reads within preview_open); the contract's PreviewDomain has no paging method, so no TS caller can exist. validate.mjs phase 2 requires every non-internal manifest row to be invoked — a command with zero possible callers would be dead surface.

removed.name: preview_close
removed.why: Internal helper: preview handles are transient (opened + closed inside preview_open/preview_thumbnail) — no registry, no lifecycle command needed.

invariants: Every command here is registered in ui/src-tauri invoke_handler and implemented under ui/src-tauri/src/commands/.
The TS connector invokes no command absent from this manifest (validate.mjs check 4/5).
The gap-method commands (repair_*) exist so the disabled surfaces throw a typed not-implemented from the bridge — the UI renders a truthful message, never a dead button.
Command names use snake_case (Rust) and are invoked with the exact same names from TS.
The `removed` array records commands/events dropped from earlier drafts with rationale — the manifest mirrors the SHIPPED surface truthfully (no dead rows).
